facts.text: RexWalk-v0 is registered with entry point rex_gym.envs.gym.walk_env:RexWalkEnv and max_episode_steps=2500
RexWalkEnv is the alternating-leg locomotion environment for the quadruped Rex
With the default signal_type 'ik' the action space is a Box of two elements bounded by -0.4 and 0.4; the 'ol' signal mode has eight elements bounded by -0.01 and 0.01
An observation is [roll, pitch, roll_rate, pitch_rate] of the robot base
The observation upper bound is 2*pi for roll and pitch and 2*pi/time_step for the two rates, and the lower bound is its negation
The default control_time_step is 0.005 s and the default action_repeat is 5
The base environment computes its simulation step as control_time_step/action_repeat, which is 0.001 s with the RexWalk defaults
The base reset sets the pybullet time step to that simulation step
The base constructor builds the observation space as a Box from the lower bound minus OBSERVATION_EPS to the upper bound plus OBSERVATION_EPS
RexWalkEnv.reset resets its flags, draws the backwards flag and the target position from Python's global random module and returns _get_observation()
RexWalkEnv.reset passes the stand initial pose and a 0.5 s reset duration to the base reset
seed(seed) replaces the environment's numpy generator with gym.utils.seeding.np_random and returns [seed]
step applies the action through rex.Step, computes the reward and termination, increments the step counter and returns (observation, reward, done, info)
The walk environment considers Rex fallen when the dot product of the world up vector and the base up vector is below 0.85
The base termination is is_fallen() or env_goal_reached or _out_of_trajectory()
RexWalkEnv sets goal_reached and is_terminating when the base x is within 0.15 of the target position
The reward weights default to distance 1.0, energy 0.0005, drift 2.0 and shake 0.005
The base reward is the sum of the weighted forward, energy, drift and shake terms
RexWalkEnv declares the render modes human and rgb_array at 66 frames per second
The clone pins numpy 1.17.3, pybullet 2.8.3, gym 0.17.1, tensorflow 1.15.5 and tensorflow-probability 0.8 in requirements.txt
The README instructs users to create a Python 3.7 environment
The README documents Rex as a 12-joint robot with 3 motors for each leg and imports the model into pyBullet

determinism.notes: seed(seed) replaces the environment's numpy generator (rex_gym_env.py:359-361), but reset() draws the backwards flag and the target position from Python's global random module (walk_env.py:133-146), so a seed does not fix a whole trajectory; pybullet's solver also gives no run-to-run equality claim.  The package fake draws both values from its own random.Random(seed), so the fake alone repeats a trajectory for one seed.

gaps: F1 is the pybullet rigid-body model of the clone; the package fake is an analytic stand-in with no contacts, friction, actuator, sensor or noise model and makes no physics claim
the fake does not model the URDF, the 12-joint motor model, the gait planner, inverse kinematics, the fall test or the reward: it advances a four-value placeholder observation and returns reward 0.0

the fake applies the registered 2500-step limit as gymnasium truncation; the upstream class alone never truncates (its step returns the legacy 4-tuple) and gym.make wraps it in a TimeLimit (rex_gym/playground/__init__.py:24-29)

the upstream reset draws the backwards flag and target position from Python's global random module (walk_env.py:133-146), so the bridge seed does not repeat an upstream trajectory; the fake draws them from random.Random(seed) and was never compared with the pybullet environment

the sim backend was not run: the clone targets Python 3.7 and pins numpy 1.17.3, pybullet 2.8.3, gym 0.17.1 and TensorFlow 1.15.5 (requirements.txt:1-7, README.md:22-26), none of them installed where the gate ran; a backend outside backends goes through gymnasium.make and needs rex_gym.playground imported
no rendering: the metadata declares human and rgb_array at 66 frames per second (walk_env.py:27) but the fake draws no frames and cap.world.render.v1 is unbound

no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0; one environment step applies action_repeat=5 physics steps of 1 ms, a 5 ms control period (walk_env.py:34-35, rex_gym_env.py:170-173), while timestep_ms names the 1 ms physics step, as FID-015 requires when the two are separated
snapshot and restore are not offered: RexWalkEnv defines no get_state or set_state
the legacy reset() signature takes no options (walk_env.py:125); the bridge falls back to reset() after seed(seed), so a non-empty options object is ignored

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop the runtime refuses every step and reset until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the last world state stays readable; the simulator has no native stop
